documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CONSULT
Visit date: 12/28/2022
Patient: Tammy Washington   DOB 04/09/1969
Referring: primary care

Reason: mild right-sided abdominal discomfort for several weeks, abnormal liver enzymes.

History: 53-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, hyperlipidemia and obesity, seen this year by dermatology for acanthosis nigricans and by sports medicine for knee and foot complaints. The discomfort is mild and intermittent. No nausea, vomiting, weight loss or change in bowel habit. Diabetes and lipids both remain above goal. She takes metformin and a statin; she has not been back to her endocrinologist in more than a year. Cholecystectomy 2014.

Medications (as listed): lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: no tobacco, no alcohol. Sedentary at a desk job, meals at irregular times.

Exam: T 98.4 F, BP 142/90, HR 82, RR 16. BMI 35. Abdomen soft, nontender; liver edge palpable a few cm below the costal margin. No jaundice, palmar erythema, spider angiomata or other signs of chronic liver disease.

Data: AST 52, ALT 63, ALP 90, T bili 0.7 (12/6). A1c 7.9, LDL 158, TG 260. Hepatitis B surface antigen negative and hepatitis C antibody nonreactive today.

Impression: Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, diagnosed clinically: mild hepatomegaly and transaminase elevation in the setting of diabetes, obesity and hypertriglyceridemia, viral hepatitis excluded, no alcohol.

Recommendations:
1. Weight loss of 7 to 10 percent of body weight is the treatment with the best evidence. Regular activity, fewer refined carbohydrates.
2. Continue her statin; it is safe in fatty liver disease.
3. Better diabetes control per primary care.
4. Repeat liver tests with her routine labs. GI follow-up as needed.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI consult reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: GI letter from 12/28 reviewed: clinical dx NASH, hep B sAg and hep C Ab negative. Added NASH to problem list. Called pt: plan is weight loss 7-10% (about 7-9 kg for her), activity, carbs. She asked about a medication for the liver - told her weight loss is the treatment GI recommends. Liver tests with routine labs.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Shingrix #2, 0.5 mL IM L deltoid. Dose 1 10/13/22 gave her a sore arm and tiredness one day, nothing else. Series complete. Tolerated well.
Pt mentioned GI letter: told her fatty liver with inflammation, wants to lose weight. Routed to PCP FYI.

orders.reason: irregular heavy menstrual bleeding with intermenstrual spotting

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Chief concern: periods.

Since about September her periods have gone haywire: they used to come monthly, 5 days, moderate. Now they come whenever, some very heavy with clots, and she spots between them. Going through pads quickly on the heavy days. No dizziness or fainting. Not sexually active, no chance of pregnancy per pt. Last Pap 2020 normal.
Liver: saw GI 12/28, told fatty liver with inflammation (NASH). Trying to cut carbs. Weight unchanged so far.
Foot: tarsal tunnel symptoms milder with the inserts.

Exam: vitals as recorded. Conjunctivae not pale. Abd soft, nontender. Pelvic deferred to gyn.

Assessment and plan
- Irregular heavy menstrual bleeding with intermenstrual spotting, age 53, with obesity and diabetes - needs endometrial evaluation. Gyn referral today. CBC.
- T2DM - fasting labs.
- NASH - liver panel with today's labs. Weight loss counseling, she's interested.
- Mixed HLD, HTN - continue current meds.
- Tarsal tunnel L - better.
f/u after gyn.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tammy, your hemoglobin is 11.2, a bit low, which fits with the heavy bleeding. Fasting sugar 162, cholesterol 220, triglycerides 250. Liver tests are in the same range as December. Gyn has your referral. If you feel lightheaded, short of breath, or the bleeding soaks a pad an hour, call us right away.

reports.text: Specimen: endometrium, office biopsy. Gross: multiple fragments of tan-red soft tissue, 1.2 cm in aggregate. Microscopic: proliferative-type endometrium with increased gland-to-stroma ratio and glandular crowding, without cytologic atypia. No carcinoma identified.
reports.conclusion: Endometrial hyperplasia without atypia. Negative for carcinoma.

documents.title: Gynecology Note
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OB/GYN outpatient note - visit 04/26/2023, addendum 05/03/2023
Pt: Tammy Washington, DOB 4/9/69. Referred by PCP.

S: 54 y/o with T2DM, HTN, HLD, obesity, prior workup for acanthosis nigricans and fatty liver. Six months of irregular, heavy menses, unpredictable timing, intermenstrual spotting. Previously regular cycles, moderate flow x5 days. No menses for the past 2 months. Most recent Pap normal. FHx: maternal grandmother with endometrial cancer.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.
O: BMI 35, BP 142/88. Bimanual: uterus enlarged, nontender. No adnexal masses.
Labs from PCP 3/14: Hgb 11.2, FBG 162, TC 220, TG 250.
Procedure: endometrial biopsy in office, tolerated well.

Addendum 5/3: pathology - endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, no carcinoma. Discussed by phone. Plan levonorgestrel IUD as first-line treatment; insertion visit scheduled June. Repeat sampling to follow on treatment.

Gynecology

documents.title: Gyn biopsy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Tammy, I got the gyn note. The biopsy showed endometrial hyperplasia without atypia - an overgrowth of the uterine lining, not cancer. The hormone IUD they recommend is the standard first treatment and usually controls the bleeding too. Let me know once it's in, and we'll recheck your blood count in the summer.

medications.sig: 52 mg levonorgestrel IUD placed by gynecology

documents.title: IUD in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI I got the hormone IUD put in on Friday (the 16th) at the gyn for the thickened lining. Some cramping the first day, fine now. They said bleeding could be irregular for a few months then should settle.

documents.title: RE: IUD in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. I added the levonorgestrel IUD to your medication list. Let's see how the bleeding goes and recheck your blood count at your August visit.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
SUBJECTIVE: Doing well. IUD since 6/16: spotting the first several weeks, now very light and much less often. No heavy bleeding since.
Since the GI visit she's been walking after dinner most nights and packing lunch; down about 3 kg on our scale. Foot symptoms gone, still wears the inserts. Meds: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, LNG-IUD.

OBJECTIVE: vitals as recorded. Weight 92 kg. Exam: well, no pallor. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abd soft nontender. Feet intact, monofilament normal.

ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, on LNG-IUD per gyn - bleeding controlled. CBC today to confirm recovery. Heavy menstrual bleeding resolved.
2. T2DM - A1c, BMP, urine albumin today. Continue metformin.
3. NASH - weight loss is the treatment; encouraged.
4. Tarsal tunnel L - resolved.
5. HTN, mixed HLD - continue.
6. Due: flu and COVID this fall. Ask about hepatitis B vaccine (diabetes) - she agrees, will start in October.
RTC 5 months.

documents.title: Your labs

documents.body: Hi Tammy, the doctor reviewed your labs. Your hemoglobin is back in the normal range. A1c is about where it was. Kidney function and urine protein normal. No changes. Your flu, COVID and hepatitis B shots can all be done at a nurse visit in October; reply here and we'll book it.

documents.title: tired + right side
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi. Over the winter I've been more tired than usual and that ache under my right ribs is back, more days than not. Not terrible. No fever, no vomiting. Should I go back to the liver doctor? I'm still walking and lost some weight so I don't get it.

documents.title: RE: tired + right side
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good thinking. With your fatty liver history I'd like GI to see you again; I've sent the referral and asked them to fit you in this month. If the pain gets severe, you get a fever, yellow eyes or skin, or vomiting, go to urgent care or the ED.

reports.text: Complete abdominal ultrasound. Liver: enlarged, diffusely increased echogenicity with posterior attenuation, consistent with hepatic steatosis. Gallbladder surgically absent; no stones in the gallbladder fossa. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation. Pancreas partially obscured by bowel gas, visualized portions normal. Spleen normal in size. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Abdominal aorta normal caliber. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Hepatic steatosis. Post-cholecystectomy. No biliary dilatation.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GI follow-up - 04/26/2024
Re: Tammy Washington (DOB 04/09/1969)

Ms. Washington returns, last seen here in December 2022 for right upper quadrant discomfort and NASH. For about six months she has had fatigue and the RUQ ache again. No alcohol. Medications include metformin and lisinopril; listed: atorvastatin 40 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: BMI 32 (down from 35). Liver enlarged on palpation. No jaundice, ascites or spider angiomata.

Labs today: AST 70, ALT 85, ALP 90, total bilirubin 1.2, albumin 4.0, platelets 220. Fasting glucose 160, A1c 7.8.
Ultrasound today: hepatic steatosis; post-cholecystectomy; no ductal dilatation.

Assessment: NASH, transaminases higher than 2022 despite some weight loss. Synthetic function and platelets preserved.

Plan: MRI of the abdomen with and without contrast to better characterize the liver. Continue weight loss efforts. Will forward results.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI follow-up note reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: GI note 4/26 reviewed: AST 70, ALT 85, bili 1.2, albumin 4.0, plt 220; US steatosis, no ductal dilatation. GI ordering MRI abdomen. Pt aware, MRI booked 5/20 per her. Will watch for report.

reports.study: MRI abdomen with and without contrast
reports.text: MRI abdomen without and with IV hepatobiliary contrast. Liver enlarged with diffuse signal loss on opposed-phase imaging, consistent with steatosis. A single 2.6 cm well-circumscribed lesion in hepatic segment 6 shows arterial phase enhancement without washout and is hypointense on the hepatobiliary phase, features of hepatocellular adenoma. No other hepatic lesion. Portal and hepatic veins patent. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation. Gallbladder surgically absent. Spleen normal in size. Pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys unremarkable. No ascites or lymphadenopathy.
reports.conclusion: 1. Single 2.6 cm segment 6 lesion consistent with hepatocellular adenoma. 2. Hepatic steatosis.

documents.title: Outside MRI report received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Outside MRI abdomen 05/20/2024 report received by fax from the imaging center, with GI cover note: "Adenoma, small. No estrogen. Continue weight loss. Repeat MRI in about 12 months - we will order. GI." Scanned. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Your MRI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Tammy, I have your MRI report and the GI note. Besides the fatty liver, the MRI found a single small growth in the liver, 2.6 cm, that looks like a hepatic adenoma. That's a benign (non-cancer) growth of liver cells. The usual plan for one this size is what GI recommends: avoid estrogen (your IUD is a progestin, not estrogen, so it's fine), keep losing weight, and repeat the MRI in about a year to make sure it stays the same. GI will order that.

I know "growth in the liver" sounds scary. Happy to talk it through on the phone or at your physical.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PREVENTIVE VISIT

55 yo F. Sorry about July, work crunch. Feels fine. The right-side ache comes and goes, milder than spring. Tiredness better. Understood the MRI result; a little anxious about the adenoma but reassured by the plan. GI to repeat MRI next spring.

Problems: T2DM, HTN, mixed hyperlipidemia, obesity, metabolic syndrome, acanthosis nigricans, NASH, hepatic adenoma, endometrial hyperplasia without atypia on LNG-IUD (gyn).
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, LNG-IUD. NKDA.
FH unchanged. SH: data entry, never smoker, no alcohol. Walks 30-40 min most days.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: vitals reviewed. BMI ~32. Well appearing. HEENT normal. Neck no thyromegaly. Lungs clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abd soft, liver edge just palpable, nontender. Skin: acanthosis at neck and axillae. Ext no edema. Feet: intact skin, pulses normal, monofilament intact. Neuro grossly normal. Mood good.

A/P:
- T2DM: A1c, CMP, urine albumin today. Metformin 1000 BID.
- HTN: office readings vary, continue lisinopril 20.
- Mixed HLD: lipids today. Atorvastatin 40.
- NASH/hepatic adenoma: per GI. LFTs in CMP.
- Endometrial hyperplasia: per gyn, IUD.
- HM: mammogram 11/2023 normal, next 11/2025. Colonoscopy 2019, next 2029. Pap 2020 normal with HPV neg, next due 2025 - gyn following. Shingrix, PCV20, Hep B done. Flu/COVID in fall. Eye exam due.
PHQ-9 1, GAD-7 2.
RTC 5-6 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs from the physical: A1c a little better than winter. LDL lower than last time, triglycerides still high. Liver enzymes are still up, around where GI had them in April, as expected with the fatty liver. Kidney, thyroid, blood counts and urine protein all normal. Keep it up - see you in January.
